sections.title: The letter erre
paragraphs: The letter (erre) /ˈere/ makes two sounds in Spanish. Its main sound is the sound /r/. You hear this sound in the word (rojo) /ˈro.xo/, which means red.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: For the first sound, touch the ridge behind your upper teeth with your tongue tip. Push air forward to make your tongue tip flap rapidly several times. For the second sound, tap your tongue tip once against that same ridge behind your teeth. Your vocal cords vibrate for both sounds. Place two fingers on your throat to feel this steady buzz.

sections.title: When to use each
paragraphs: This letter makes the rolled sound /r/ when written as double r, as in (perro) /ˈpe.ro/. It also makes the sound /r/ at the start of a word, or after l, n, or s. The letter makes the single tap sound /ɾ/ between two vowels, as in (pero) /ˈpe.ɾo/. It also makes the sound /ɾ/ after another consonant, as in (tres) /tɾes/, or at the end of a syllable.

sections.title: Mistakes to avoid
paragraphs: Do not pull your tongue back into your mouth, as in the English word red. Keep your tongue forward against the hard ridge behind your teeth. Do not blow air without tongue contact, as in the English word rose. Tap your tongue tip firmly against your upper gum instead.
